title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: scope just-in-time audit to users and groups
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's planned audit-scoping change, December rollout and administrator recommendations. The controls table reaches the correct settings page but should extend its audit-control path to the Devices tab and Audit covered user activities setting.

claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns Microsoft Purview Endpoint Data Loss Prevention.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview: Endpoint Data Loss Prevention - Allow customer to scope JIT Audit to specific user or user group

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap target is December CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "December CY2026"

claims.claim: The release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-09-14T23:03:47.
Microsoft plans to let customers include users or groups in JIT audit scope.
claims.quote: Enable customers to include or exclude users/user groups from Just‑In‑Time (JIT) Audit

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap also describes excluding users or groups from JIT audit.
claims.quote: Enable customers to include or exclude users/user groups from Just‑In‑Time (JIT) Audit

claims.claim: The roadmap says audits will be generated only for selected users or groups.
claims.quote: ensuring audits are generated only for the selected users or groups.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The notice says JIT audit logging must be explicitly configured for included users or groups.
claims.quote: With this update, audit logging must be explicitly configured so that only users or groups included in the audit scope have their activities logged.

claims.claim: Previously, enabling JIT automatically logged activity for users not targeted by policies.
claims.quote: Previously, when Just-in-time protection was turned on, user activities were logged automatically for users who were not targeted by policies.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance / At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The notice places Audit covered user activities on Devices under Settings > Data loss prevention > Just-in-time protection.
claims.quote: Just-in-time audit behavior is now managed through the Audit covered user activities setting under Settings > Data loss prevention > Just-in-time protection. Under the Devices tab, turn on Audit covered user activities.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment / Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Users included in audit scope see no enforcement actions.
claims.quote: Users included in audit scope will not see enforcement actions

claims.claim: Audit-scope users have their activities recorded in Activity explorer.
claims.quote: Users included in audit scope will not see enforcement actions, and their activities will be recorded in Activity explorer.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment / Autonomy & actions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Block-scope users are prevented from completing actions while files are evaluated for sensitive information.
claims.quote: Users included in block scope will be prevented from completing actions while files are evaluated for sensitive information.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Block-scope activity is also recorded in Activity explorer.
claims.quote: Users included in block scope will be prevented from completing actions while files are evaluated for sensitive information. Their activities are recorded in Activity explorer.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment / Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Users outside both scopes have no JIT-covered activity recorded.
claims.quote: Users not included in audit or block scope will not have activities covered by Just-in-time protection recorded.

claims.claim: The notice lists printing as an audited activity.
claims.quote: Audited activities include printing

claims.claim: The notice lists transfers to removable media as audited.
claims.quote: transfers to removable media or network shares

claims.claim: The notice lists transfers to network shares as audited.
claims.quote: transfers to removable media or network shares

claims.claim: The notice lists copying or moving files using Remote Desktop Protocol as audited.
claims.quote: copying or moving files using Remote Desktop Protocol or an unapproved Bluetooth app

claims.claim: The notice lists copying or moving files using an unapproved Bluetooth app as audited.
claims.quote: copying or moving files using Remote Desktop Protocol or an unapproved Bluetooth app

claims.claim: The notice lists uploading files to a restricted cloud service domain as audited.
claims.quote: uploading files to a restricted cloud service domain.

claims.claim: The notice was updated on 14 September 2026.
claims.quote: Updated September 14, 2026: We have updated the timeline.

claims.claim: The notice schedules rollout to begin in mid-December 2026.
claims.quote: Global: We will begin rolling out in mid-December 2026 (previously mid-September)

claims.claim: The notice expects rollout completion by end of December 2026.
claims.quote: expect to complete by end of December 2026 (previously end of September).

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance / Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection reaches the page holding audit and block scoping.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal.
2. Select Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection.
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path and the corresponding rendered table path to 'Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection > Devices > Audit covered user activities'. MC1387575 supplies the final tab and setting; retain the note explaining that Learn does not yet document them.

claims.claim: No documented PowerShell, Graph or other API was found to configure JIT audit and block scope.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview "just-in-time protection" PowerShell Graph API settings audit scope; "JIT" "Set-Dlp". Read both JIT pages and Purview API search excerpts; no operation sets Endpoint JIT audit or block scope.

claims.claim: The Devices control is at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection > Choose which locations to monitor > Devices.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal.
2. Select Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection.
3. Under Choose which locations to monitor, select the checkbox next to Devices.

claims.claim: No documented API was found for setting the Devices monitored location for JIT protection.
claims.quote: Searched: "just-in-time" "Devices" "PowerShell" "DLP"; "JIT" "Set-Dlp". Read both JIT pages and search results distinguishing Azure VM JIT APIs; no Endpoint DLP monitored-location operation was documented.

claims.claim: The existing Devices checkbox chooses a monitored location rather than which users receive JIT audit.
claims.quote: Under Choose which locations to monitor, select the checkbox next to Devices.

claims.claim: The notice describes audit configuration using user or group selection.
claims.quote: The feature introduces additional admin configuration controls for scoping audit behavior, which may be applied using user or group selection.

claims.claim: The affected administrators manage Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP and JIT protection settings.
claims.quote: Who is affected: Admins managing Microsoft Purview Endpoint Data Loss Prevention and Just-in-time protection settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment / Security & identity; Why it matters
claims.claim: The notice identifies compliance and investigation workflows as depending on the collected JIT audit data.
claims.quote: The change alters how Just-in-time audit data is collected and reviewed for compliance and investigation workflows.

claims.claim: Learn supplies an Advanced hunting query that reports antimalware client versions.
claims.quote: AntiMalwareClientVersion = InitiatingProcessVersionInfoProductVersion

claims.claim: Learn documents using the Diagnostics page to check a device's JIT prerequisite and antimalware version.
claims.quote: You can also go to Data Loss Prevention > Diagnostics page, and select Endpoint DLP not working card to check whether a specific device meets JIT prerequisite.

claims.claim: The notice identifies Endpoint Data Loss Prevention and Activity explorer as affected services.
claims.quote:
Platforms/Services: 

- Microsoft Purview- Endpoint Data Loss Prevention- Activity explorer.

claims.claim: JIT blocking for in-scope users is existing behavior rather than new enforcement introduced by audit scoping.
claims.quote: JIT block: After you enable JIT, Endpoint DLP blocks the activity and generates an event in activity explorer for every JIT candidate file.

claims.claim: Users outside JIT scope have no new device-facing enforcement from this audit-scoping change.
claims.quote:
DLP confirms that the user is in scope for JIT. If yes, evaluation continues. If not, the process ends at step 5.
5. JIT doesn't block the activity. No notification is shown, and a JIT audit event is logged.
